Madam Chair, I have the honor to introduce the report of WHO on health statistics. This report comes at a critical moment. Although advances have been recorded in selected areas, current trajectories indicate that most targets are off track and will require accelerated evidence-based and equity-oriented action. Updated analysis highlights mixed trends in communicable diseases. Notable progress in reducing new HIV infections and stabilizing tuberculosis after pandemic-related disruptions is tempered by continued increase in malaria incidence in several high-burden settings. There are advances in non-communicable disease prevention and control, but not enough to reach global targets. Women's health and wellbeing remain central concerns. Maternal mortality remains unacceptably high, and progress must accelerate to meet global commitments. Access to reproductive health services has largely stalled. Anemia among women of reproductive age continues to pose a significant public health challenge, and violence against women and girls remains high, underscoring the need for sustained multisectoral efforts and improved measurement of underlying risk factors and vulnerabilities. Beyond the sector-specific outcomes, the report emphasizes the foundational role of strong statistical system. The emerging uncertainties of a major survey programs and the decline in external financing have exposed persistent fragility in data availability, particularly in low and lower middle-income countries.
